Name: FileTransformingComposite
Purpose: The template FileTransformingComposite describes the transformation of several files into a single file by a single activity.
Context: The template is useful when one operation reads several files and writes one, for instance when several files are combined into an archive.
Design considerations: The ability to submit together all the FileTransforming records of one operation, so that they are stored, or rejected, as a whole.
Details:
FileTransformingComposite does not have a graph of its own: it is a composite of the template FileTransforming, made of several FileTransforming records submitted together. All the records share the resulting file, transformed_file, and the activity transforming; each record describes one of the input files, file.
A composite record states how many records it groups and of which type; each of its elements is a complete FileTransforming record, linked to the composite. The composite is submitted as a single request, so its elements are stored together, or not at all.
An example is the Unix command tar -czf archive.tgz file1 file2 file3{.sh}, which writes the three files into the single archive archive.tgz.
